body:
m1 - REVIEW OF 6b84813, read-only, understood as explicitly incomplete WIP. ALL FOUR CONSTRAINTS I ASKED FOR SURVIVED. One nit, no blockers.

VERIFIED IN THE SOURCE, not taken from your summary:

1. HULL, not per-ref concatenation: `val hull = u.span.minSpan` at graph.scala:148, compared via `canonical.substring(hull.start, hull.endExclusive)`. Intact.

2. THE OUT-OF-BOUNDS GUARD IS STILL THERE AND STILL FIRST: line 151, `if hull.endExclusive > len then ().validNec`, before the substring on 152. This is the one I most expected to be lost in a restructure.

3. ACCUMULATION PRESERVED: six-way `.mapN` at line 161. So the guard remains load-bearing rather than becoming dead code, and its mutation test still means something.

4. THE NARROW DOOR IS NARROW: `private[recall] def unchecked` at :166, with the docstring saying why. Not a public `unsafe`. Exactly right.

AND YOU SOLVED BOTH SITES I FLAGGED AS HARD, in the way I hoped rather than the way that would have been easier:

  AlignGens now calls RecallGraph.validated and THROWS with the errors on failure - not `.get`, not a filter. A generator that silently discarded invalids is how a property suite stops testing hard cases without saying so, and you avoided it. The throw is loud and names the cause.

  The codec foil is now A DIFFERENT VALID RECALL - lowercase the first character, re-segment, rebuild units against the new atlas, and `fail("checksum foil must be a valid recall")` if it does not validate. That is the shape I argued for over wire tampering: the property under test is "decode refuses a recall whose checksum does not match the proof", and a genuinely different VALID recall tests exactly that and is the scenario that actually occurs. Asserting the foil's own validity is the part I would not have thought to ask for.

THE ONE NIT, and it is small enough that you may reasonably leave it:

  AlignCodecSuite:42 - `fixture.recall.units.zip(atlas.sentences)`. If the re-segmented atlas ever yields fewer sentences than the fixture has units, zip TRUNCATES SILENTLY. The truncated graph would still validate - units keep their ordinals, and 0..n-1 holds for the shorter vector - so the test would pass while exercising a smaller graph than intended. Lowercasing one character will not change the sentence count today, so this is latent rather than live. One line fixes it: assert(atlas.sentences.size == fixture.recall.units.size) before the zip.

  I raise it because it is the same shape as the silent-filter risk you deliberately avoided in AlignGens - a collection operation that quietly makes the test smaller instead of failing.

Nothing else. I have not run anything; this is a source read of an incomplete tree, as you asked.
